elbow-rom-normative.description: Normative range-of-motion reference for the approximate 0-145 deg teaching range. Zwerus EL, Willigenburg NW, Scholtes VA, Somford MP, Eygendaal D, van den Bekerom MPJ. 'Normative values and affecting factors for the elbow range of motion.' Shoulder & Elbow 11(3):215-224 (2019). doi:10.1177/1758573217728711, PMCID PMC6555111. Mean active flexion of the dominant hand was 146 deg across 352 healthy adults; the paper cites a literature range of 130-154 deg and reports that elbow range varies with age, sex and BMI. It supports the reasonableness of the teaching range only: it does not validate the geometry, axis or limits of this 3D model, which remain pending expert review.

source.elbow_hinge.text: The elbow bends and straightens in one direction, similar to a door hinge.

intro.subtitle.text: How different joints allow different kinds of movement.

intro.where.text: You have joints like these all over your body. We will look at four kinds.

fixed.text.text: The bones of the skull meet at fixed joints. These bones do not move against each other.

pivot.label.text: Pivot joint · top of the neck

pivot.text.text: The upper bone turns around the one below it. Your head turns with it.

ball.text.shoulder.text: At the shoulder, the rounded top of the upper arm bone sits in a hollow of the shoulder bone, so the arm can move in many directions.

hinge.axis.text: This blue line shows the direction the elbow bends around. We call that line the axis.

hinge.axis_note.text: Blue line: the hinge axis fitted to this 3D model.

hinge.flexion.text: When the elbow bends, that is called flexion.

hinge.extension.text: When it straightens again, that is called extension.

hinge.range_note.text: 0-145 deg is an approximate teaching range for this model; adult elbow flexion varies between people (see Sources).

hinge.try.text: Your turn: bend and straighten the elbow.

hinge.try_prompt.text: Drag the forearm, or use the slider.

hinge.support.text: A joint capsule and ligaments surround the elbow.

hinge.bands_note.text: The thin coloured lines mark where the ligaments run. They are a guide, not real tissue.

hinge.knee.text: The knee is another hinge joint.

recap.compare.text: Fixed: no movement · Pivot: turning · Ball and socket: many directions · Hinge: one direction

explore.fixed.explanation.text: These bones barely move. A fixed joint holds bones firmly together.

explore.pivot.title.text: Pivot joint · top of the neck

explore.pivot.instruction.text: Drag left and right to turn the head.

explore.pivot.explanation.text: The head turns around the bone below it. A pivot joint allows rotation.

explore.ball.instruction.text: Drag in any direction to move the arm.

explore.ball.explanation.text: The arm moves in many directions, not just one. That is a ball-and-socket joint.

explore.hinge.instruction.text: Drag to bend and straighten the elbow.

explore.hinge.explanation.text: Bending is flexion. Straightening is extension. A hinge joint does both, in one direction.

recall.q.skull.text: These skull bones hardly move at all.

recall.q.neck.text: The head turns around the bone below it.

recall.q.shoulder.text: The arm moves in many directions.

recall.q.elbow.text: This joint bends and straightens in one direction.

recall.a.skull.text: Fixed: the bones hold firm, so there is little or no movement.

recall.a.neck.text: Pivot: one bone rotates around another.

recall.a.shoulder.text: Ball-and-socket: the rounded end sits in a socket, so it moves many ways.

recall.a.elbow.text: Hinge: it bends and straightens in one main direction.

hook.elbow.text: Your elbow mainly bends and straightens.

hook.question.text: Both are joints. So why do they move so differently?

concept.meet.text: A joint is a place where bones meet.

ui.teaching_view.text: Teaching view: the moving marks show the kind of movement.

ui.explore_teaching_note.text: This shows the movement pattern. The bones are real; the movement is a demonstration.

a11y.pivot.bones.text: Close view of the first two neck bones, seen from the front and right. They are highlighted; the skull is dimmed behind them.

hinge.return.text: The elbow settles back to rest.

narr.concept.meet.text: A joint is any place where bones meet. Most joints are two bones meeting; here at the elbow, three bones come together.

narr.concept.different.text: How the bones meet at a joint decides how that joint can move. Change the shape of the join and you change the movement.

narr.intro.map.text: You have joints like these all over your body. We will look at four kinds, and at what each shape allows.

narr.intro.title.text: Every time you move, bones move against each other at a joint. Different joints allow very different movements.

narr.hook.shoulder.text: Start with the shoulder. Your arm can swing forward, out to the side, and round in a circle.

narr.hook.elbow.text: Now the elbow, on the same arm. It does one thing: it bends and it straightens.

narr.hook.question.text: Both are joints in the same arm. So why does one move in every direction and the other in only one?

narr.fixed.travel.text: Go up to the top of the head. The skull looks like a single piece, but it is several separate bones meeting along wavy lines.

narr.fixed.bones.text: These are two of those bones, and this is the line where they meet. Look at how the edges follow each other.

narr.fixed.try.text: Watch the join itself. Nothing slides, nothing bends, nothing shifts at all.

narr.fixed.why.text: The edges of these bones lock into each other, and tough fibres hold them tightly together. There is no gap for them to slide in, so they cannot move against each other.

narr.fixed.name.text: A join that holds two bones still like this is called a fixed joint. Its job is strength, not movement: together these bones make one solid case around the brain.

narr.fixed.task.text: Try it yourself. See whether you can move these two bones apart.

narr.pivot.travel.text: Now down to the top of the neck, just under the skull, where the head meets the backbone.

pivot.bones.head.text: One bone on top of another

narr.pivot.bones.text: At the top of the neck, one small bone sits on top of another. Nothing is moving yet. The lower bone is the one that stays still.

narr.pivot.rotate.text: Now the upper bone turns around the one below it, and your head turns with it.

narr.pivot.why.text: The upper bone turns around one line running straight up through both bones. Turning around that line is the only movement this shape allows, which is why the head swivels here rather than bending.

narr.pivot.name.text: A joint where one bone turns around another like this is called a pivot joint.

narr.pivot.task.text: Try it yourself. Turn the head as if you were looking over one shoulder.

ball.travel.head.text: Where the arm meets the body

narr.ball.travel.text: Back up to the shoulder, where the arm meets the body.

ball.bones.head.text: A round end and a hollow

narr.ball.bones.text: The top of the upper-arm bone is a smooth, rounded ball. Beside it, the shoulder blade has a shallow hollow, and the ball rests in it.

narr.ball.move.text: From this one joint, the arm can move in many directions: forward, backwards, out sideways, and right round.

narr.ball.why.text: A rounded end sitting in a hollow can roll and turn in every direction at once. Nothing holds it to a single line, so the arm is not limited to one direction the way the elbow is.

narr.ball.name.text: A rounded end sitting in a hollow like this is called a ball-and-socket joint.

narr.ball.task.text: Try it yourself. Move the arm in two different directions.

narr.hinge.travel.text: Down the same arm now, to the elbow.

narr.hinge.source.text: The elbow bends and straightens in one direction, the way a door swings on its hinges.

narr.hinge.bones.text: The elbow is where the upper-arm bone meets two bones in the forearm.

narr.hinge.axis.text: This blue line shows the direction the elbow bends around. We call that line the axis.

narr.hinge.flexion.text: Watch the forearm come up. When the elbow bends like this, the movement is called flexion.

narr.hinge.extension.text: And as it straightens again, that movement is called extension.

hinge.why.head.text: Why it bends only one way

narr.hinge.why.text: Look at the shape of the join. The end of the upper-arm bone is like a spool, and the forearm bone wraps around it. A spool can only turn about its own line, so the elbow can only bend and straighten.

narr.hinge.name.text: A joint that bends and straightens around one line like this is called a hinge joint.

narr.hinge.support.text: A joint capsule and ligaments wrap around the elbow. They hold the bones together and keep the movement on that one line.

narr.hinge.return.text: The elbow settles back to rest.

narr.hinge.knee.text: The knee is another hinge joint. It is bigger, but it does the same thing: it bends and straightens one way.

narr.compare.pullback.text: Four joints, in one body, with four different ways of moving. Look at each one again.

narr.compare.fixed.text: The skull: edges locked together, so almost no movement.

narr.compare.pivot.text: The top of the neck: one bone turning around another.

narr.compare.ball.text: The shoulder: a round end in a hollow, so movement in many directions.

narr.compare.hinge.text: The elbow: bending and straightening around one line.

narr.compare.together.text: Four different shapes, four different movements. The shape of the join decides what the joint can do.

narr.recall.open.text: Your turn again. This time you name each joint from the way it moves.

narr.map.intro.text: Here they are together, in one body.

narr.map.all.text: Four joins, four shapes, four kinds of movement. The shape of the join is what decides.

explore.fixed.task.text: Try to move the two skull bones apart.

explore.fixed.done.text: They barely move, and they spring straight back. That is a fixed joint.

explore.pivot.task.text: Turn the head as if you were looking over one shoulder.

explore.pivot.done.text: The head turned, and the bone below stayed still. That is a pivot joint.

explore.ball.task.text: Move the arm in two different directions.

explore.ball.done.text: One joint, more than one direction. That is a ball-and-socket joint.

explore.hinge.task.text: Bend the elbow until it is about half-way — around 90 degrees.

explore.hinge.done.text: That is flexion. Straighten it again and that is extension — one line, two directions.

ui.start_thesis.text: How the shape of a join decides the movement.
